searchDocs.title: Moon orbit graphics​
searchDocs.content: Before Factorio 2.1.20, it was not possible to render orbit lines that did not center on the main star. To get around this issue, PlanetsLib added features to enable placing sprites on the starmap, in addition to a Python script(helper_scripts/generate_orbit_graphics.py) to generate sprites ressembling orbits. With 2.1.20, this feature is largely obsolete, but it is still supported for developers that wish to create orbits with an appearance different from vanilla orbits.  Example​  orbit = { orientation = 0.75, distance = 2, parent = { type = "planet", name = parent_planet, }, draw_orbit = true, -- OR sprite = { type = "sprite", filename = "__Cerys-Moon-of-Fulgora__/graphics/icons/orbit.png", size = 379, scale = 0.25, }, },

searchDocs.title: Rocket Part Recipes
searchDocs.content: Rocket Part Recipes You can use the library to assign unique rocket part recipes to rocket silos placed on a specified planet to increase or decrease the difficulty of launching rockets on the planet. Rocket silos with their recipe fixed to the vanilla rocket-part recipe are targeted by PlanetsLib. To implement: Use the helper function PlanetsLib.assign_rocket_part_recipe(planet,recipe,lock_silo(default = true)) to assign a recipe to a planet, and optionally determine if the rocket silo has its recipe locked on that planet. planet and recipe may each be a name or a prototype. The first planet assigned a recipe receives a hidden PlanetsLib-is-<planet> surface condition, restricting the recipe to that planet. If the same recipe is assigned to a second planet, PlanetsLib removes that condition and marks the recipe as shared. The restriction is not reapplied, even if the second planet is later assigned a different recipe.lock_silo defaults to true. Passing false is preserved and leaves the silo unlocked.PlanetsLib stores rocket part recipe assignments in a mod-data prototype named Planetslib-planet-rocket-part-recipe. Planets with their own system for assigning rocket part recipes are exempted with the assigned recipe name _other. Muluna and Maraxsis are currently exempted in this manner to maintain backwards compatibility with those mods.PlanetsLib stores silo recipe lock data in a mod-data prototype named Planetslib-planet-lock-rocket-silos. For planets with undefined lock behavior, PlanetsLib will check if a planet has multiple valid rocket silo recipes before unlocking the silo. If only one valid recipe exists, PlanetsLib will lock the silo on placement.Planets without an assigned recipe default to the vanilla rocket-part recipe.

searchDocs.title: Recipe Events
searchDocs.content: Recipe Events PlanetsLib includes one event that recipes can hook into using RecipePrototype::PlanetsLib_recipe_effects. This event adds items to the machine's ingredient inventory on craft. Additional events may be added in the future. RecipePrototype field: PlanetsLib_recipe_effects [table]​ returned_ingredients [table(ItemProduct)] When this field is defined, returned items are inserted into the crafting machine's input. The field must be defined before data-final-fixes. PlanetsLib sets raise_on_crafted on the recipe and adds a tooltip describing the return.Only items are supported. Defining type = "fluid" raises an error during data-final-fixes.Supported fields: name (ItemID) — The item to return. It should match an ingredient of the recipe so PlanetsLib can track its production statistics.type — Must be "item".amount (number) — The number of items returned per craft, or per batch when using batch_count.independent_probability (number, 0–1) — Rolls separately for this returned ingredient on every craft.shared_probability ({min, max}, 0–1) — Uses the craft's shared roll. The ingredient is returned when the roll is between min and max, inclusive. min defaults to 0 and max to 1.ignored_by_productivity (number) — On a productivity-bonus craft, PlanetsLib returns amount - ignored_by_productivity instead of amount. This returns the base amount on a normal craft without duplicating the ignored part on bonus crafts.batch_count (positive number) — On a normal craft, instead of returning amount every craft, PlanetsLib inserts amount * batch_count items with probability 1 / batch_count. This reduces the frequency of insertions without changing the expected return rate. (Earlier documentation called this field batch_size; the implementation uses batch_count.) If neither probability field is set, the ingredient is returned on every craft.PlanetsLib derives the internal fields add_to_stats, amount_minus_ignored_by_productivity, inverse_batch_count, and no_probability during data-final-fixes. Do not set these yourself.When the returned item matches a recipe ingredient, PlanetsLib sets that ingredient's ignored_by_stats to its full amount. Do not rely on a custom ignored_by_stats value for that ingredient. Known limitations​ The tooltip displays shared_probability as a percentage ((max - min) * 100), but independent_probability as the raw 0–1 value. This is a cosmetic inconsistency.When batching skips an insertion, the skipped return is not reflected in the machine's production statistics. Returned items are also not subtracted from consumption statistics.The derived add_to_stats value is currently unused by the runtime handler. Example​ ingredients = { {type="item", name="cellulose", amount=15}, {type="item", name="alumina-crushed", amount=1}, }, results = { {type="fluid", name="petroleum-gas", amount=20}, {type="fluid", name="tar", amount=8}, }, PlanetsLib_recipe_effects = { returned_ingredients = { {type="item", name="alumina-crushed", amount=1,shared_probability = {min=0,max=0.9},ignored_by_productivity=1}, }, },

searchDocs.title: Shared prototypes​
searchDocs.content: Every planet that uses this feature shares the same ground digger prototypes. There is one prototype per eligible mining drill, named <drill>-ground-digger (for example, placing an electric-mining-drill produces an electric-mining-drill-ground-digger).  The naming scheme deliberately matches the prototypes used by Muluna, Moon of Nauvis, so saves that placed those entities keep working.

searchDocs.title: Muluna compatibility​
searchDocs.content: PlanetsLib requires planet-muluna newer than 2.7.40. Versions up to 2.7.40 include their own ground digger implementation that uses the same <drill>-ground-digger prototype names, so PlanetsLib refuses to load when one of those versions is active. Update planet-muluna to continue using this feature.  Because the prototypes are shared, the planet's recipe cannot be baked into the prototype. It is assigned at runtime when the digger is placed, and then locked. As a consequence, all ground diggers accept the crafting categories of every recipe registered with this feature, but each individual machine only ever crafts the recipe of the planet it was placed on.  Diggers are also restricted to planets that enabled the feature: PlanetsLib adds a hidden surface property to each participating planet, and every digger prototype requires it. A digger blueprint therefore cannot be built on a planet that hasn't called this function.  Placement also respects the mining drill's own surface conditions. If the drill cannot be placed on the planet (for example, a chemical burner drill on an oxygen-less planet), it will not be converted into a ground digger there. Builds in remote view are placed as ground-digger ghosts without the reach limit; the ghost becomes a recipe-bearing digger when it is built.

searchDocs.title: Eligible mining drills​
searchDocs.content: By default, every mining drill that meets all of the following criteria gets a ground digger variant:  It does not output fluids (pumpjacks are mining drills).It can mine ordinary solid resources: its resource_categories includes basic-solid, or is unset. Drills that can only be placed on specific resource sites, such as pumpjacks or anomaly collectors, are skipped.It has a square selection box.It is placeable by an item.It does not set PlanetsLib_do_not_generate_variants.Its name does not contain a quality or resource name. This skips per-quality and per-resource copies of drills. The check is a substring match, so a drill whose name contains a quality or resource name for another reason is also skipped.  These criteria apply to every drill, including drills listed explicitly in options.drills; listing a drill cannot make a resource-site-only drill eligible.  Any energy source is allowed, so non-electric drills (for example, burner mining drills) are eligible by default. A digger keeps the energy source of the drill it is copied from; diggers with an electric energy source default to no drain (0 MW), matching mining drills.  Ground digger variants are assembling machines that share the drill's appearance, health, and other properties. Mining drills that can be used as ground diggers mention this in their Factoriopedia description, linking to the generated digger variant.

searchDocs.title: Recipe requirements​
searchDocs.content: The configured recipe must exist and should be unlockable by the player (for example, through a technology). PlanetsLib does not unlock it automatically. Ground diggers also benefit from mining drill productivity research, which is applied to the recipe automatically.

searchDocs.title: Build warning​
searchDocs.content: Because ground diggers can replace a mining drill placed without nearby resources, the vanilla warning shown in that situation is misleading. PlanetsLib blanks the cant-build-reason.no-resource-for-drill locale key so the warning is not shown.

searchDocs.title: Known limitations​
searchDocs.content: drills and blacklist control which digger prototypes are generated and which drills the custom build path converts. Because the prototypes are shared, a digger generated for another planet can still be built on a planet that blacklists that drill (for example, from a blueprint or by script). PlanetsLib will not assign or lock a recipe for such a blacklisted placement, so filter those placements in your own scripts if they need a recipe.Placement collision checks are best effort. PlanetsLib combines a prototype collision check with an area scan, but some collisions, especially for non-standard drill sizes, may not be detected. Script-created diggers should not rely on PlanetsLib to validate their placement.

searchDocs.title: Example​
searchDocs.content: -- data.lua or data-updates.lua PlanetsLib.enable_ground_diggers("muluna", "muluna-regolith-digging")   With the call above, every eligible mining drill placed on muluna without nearby resources becomes a ground digger that crafts muluna-regolith-digging. To limit diggers to specific drills, or to exclude some:  PlanetsLib.enable_ground_diggers("muluna", "muluna-regolith-digging", { drills = { "electric-mining-drill", "big-mining-drill" }, blacklist = { "seafloor-drill" }, })

searchDocs.title: Storage extraction and transfer​
searchDocs.content: If a mod author has abandoned their mod, and another developer decides to fork their mod without the original author's involvement, the following remote interfaces can be used to transfer storage from saves containing the old mod to the new fork. These interfaces are intended to be used by players with /c to manually transfer storage from a mod to PlanetsLib's storage, then load the fork and transfer the cached storage from PlanetsLib's storage to the fork.  remote.call("PlanetsLib_transfer_storage","save",mod_name,storage_data): Saves the table storage_data to PlanetsLib's storage under the key mod_name.remote.call("PlanetsLib_transfer_storage","get",mod_name): Returns the storage table stored in PlanetsLib's storage under the key mod_name.remote.call("PlanetsLib_transfer_storage","purge",mod_name): Deletes the storage table stored in PlanetsLib's storage under the key mod_name.  These interfaces are used by the player. In your fork, add a variation of these instructions to explain to players how to transfer their data to the new mod.  Load save with the old mod loaded. Enter command /c __old-mod__ remote.call("PlanetsLib_transfer_storage","save","old-mod",storage). Save the game.Load save again with the old mod replaced with the new fork. Enter command /c __new-mod__ storage = remote.call("PlanetsLib_transfer_storage","get","old-mod").Delete cached storage with /c __new-mod__ remote.call("PlanetsLib_transfer_storage","purge","old-mod").  If the structure of your fork's storage differs from the original mod, you may need to add an additional function for the player to run to correct the storage, as might be run in a migration.

searchDocs.title: Entity Fields
searchDocs.content: Entity Fields EntityPrototype::PlanetsLib_pipette_result(string) — Defines the entity summoned when using the pipette tool on this entity. Is mutually exclusive with EntityPrototype::placeable_by. This field only affects pipette behavior, and does not make this entity placeable by the entity's pipette result. A wrapper for PlanetsLib.constants.pipette_result. In data-final-fixes, manipulate this mod-data table directly.EntityPrototype::PlanetsLib_do_not_generate_variants(boolean) — When true, PlanetsLib's built-in data-stage variant generators skip this prototype. This is honored by ground-digger generation, rocket-lift/rocket-part multiplier variants, and PlanetsLib.create_planet_entity_variant. PlanetsLib.create_planet_entity_variant sets it automatically on generated variants to prevent recursive variant generation; set it manually on prototypes that are already variants. PlanetsLib.create_planet_entity_variant also recognizes the generated -PlanetsLib- name suffix, so overriding the flag through new_properties cannot re-enable variant-of-variant generation.

searchDocs.title: Composite "dual item" icons​
searchDocs.content: PlanetsLib.dual_icon and PlanetsLib.dual_icon_reversed build a composite icon out of the icons of two or three existing prototypes. This is useful for recipes or technologies that are best recognised as a combination of existing items—for example, a recipe that turns one item into another.  PlanetsLib.dual_icon(item_1, item_2, item_3) — Returns an array of IconData. Up to three icons are composed: item_1 is drawn largest at the bottom, with item_2 (and the optional item_3) layered over it at a smaller scale.PlanetsLib.dual_icon_reversed(item_1, item_2) — Returns an array of IconData, composing two icons using a layout mirrored relative to PlanetsLib.dual_icon.  The arguments are prototype names (strings), not prototype tables. Each name is looked up automatically as a surface, tool, capsule, fluid, planet, or item prototype; when a name matches more than one type, the precedence is surface > tool > capsule > fluid > planet > item.  If a prototype has neither an icon nor an icons field—or if the name does not match any prototype—a placeholder icon is substituted and a message is logged.  -- A recipe that produces "water" from "my-item": data.raw.recipe["my-recipe"].icons = PlanetsLib.dual_icon("my-item", "water") -- Three icons (for example two inputs and one output): data.raw.recipe["my-recipe"].icons = PlanetsLib.dual_icon("my-item", "water", "steam") -- The mirrored two-icon layout: data.raw.recipe["my-other-recipe"].icons = PlanetsLib.dual_icon_reversed("rocket-fuel", "aluminum-crushed")

searchDocs.title: Melting recipe icons​
searchDocs.content: PlanetsLib.melting_icon(metal, ore, catalyst) builds an icon in the style of the vanilla Space Age recipes that melt an ore together with calcite into a molten metal: the catalyst and the ore are shown small at the top, with the molten product drawn large across the front. It is useful for mods that add their own melting recipes.  metal — string — prototype name of the molten product; drawn largest.ore — string — prototype name of the ore being melted.catalyst — string — optional prototype name of the catalyst. Defaults to "calcite".  Like PlanetsLib.dual_icon, each argument is a prototype name (not a table or an icon path). The prototype type is detected automatically and the icon is taken from the prototype's icon/icons field; if a name cannot be resolved, a placeholder is substituted and a message is logged.  -- calcite + alumina -> molten aluminum: data.raw.recipe["aluminum-ore-melting"].icons = PlanetsLib.melting_icon("molten-aluminum", "alumina")

searchDocs.title: Asteroid crushing recipe icons​
searchDocs.content: These helpers build icons arrays in the style of the vanilla Space Age asteroid-crushing recipes. Unlike PlanetsLib.dual_icon and PlanetsLib.melting_icon, their arguments are sprite paths (strings), not prototype names.

searchDocs.title: PlanetsLib.crushing_recipe_icons(icon_dir, icon_size)​
searchDocs.content: Returns an array of IconData resembling a basic asteroid-crushing recipe, using PlanetsLib's copper-colored crushing symbol. The supplied icon is drawn small over the crushing symbol.  icon_dir — string — sprite path of the icon to crush (the ore or asteroid chunk).icon_size — integer — optional size of icon_dir in pixels. Defaults to 64. The icon is drawn at the same apparent size regardless of the value, so a 128-pixel or 256-pixel source looks identical to a 64-pixel one.  The first entry uses icon_dir (shifted up slightly) and the second uses __PlanetsLib__/graphics/icons/generic-crushing.png.

searchDocs.title: PlanetsLib.asteroid_crushing_recipe_icons(icon_dir, icon_size)​
searchDocs.content: Identical to PlanetsLib.crushing_recipe_icons, but uses the yellow __PlanetsLib__/graphics/icons/asteroid-crushing.png symbol. It takes the same arguments.  -- A basic crushing recipe for a custom ore: data.raw.recipe["my-ore-crushing"].icons = PlanetsLib.crushing_recipe_icons("__my-mod__/graphics/icons/my-ore.png", 64) -- The same layout with the asteroid-crushing symbol: data.raw.recipe["my-asteroid-crushing"].icons = PlanetsLib.asteroid_crushing_recipe_icons("__my-mod__/graphics/icons/my-asteroid-chunk.png")

searchDocs.title: PlanetsLib.advanced_crushing_recipe_icons(asteroid_icon, product_1, product_2, variant)​
searchDocs.content: Returns an array of five IconData entries resembling an advanced asteroid-crushing recipe: four product icons are placed in quadrants at scale 0.25, with the asteroid icon drawn over them at scale 0.4.  asteroid_icon — string — sprite path of the asteroid shown on top.product_1 — string — sprite path of the first product.product_2 — string — sprite path of the second product.variant — string — optional arrangement of the four product icons. Defaults to "checkerboard": "checkerboard" — the products alternate diagonally (product_1 bottom-left and top-right, product_2 top-left and bottom-right)."horizontal" — product_1 fills the top row and product_2 the bottom row."vertical" — product_1 fills the left column and product_2 the right column.  Any other value raises an error naming the valid variants.  data.raw.recipe["my-advanced-crushing"].icons = PlanetsLib.advanced_crushing_recipe_icons( "__my-mod__/graphics/icons/my-asteroid-chunk.png", "__my-mod__/graphics/icons/product-a.png", "__my-mod__/graphics/icons/product-b.png", "vertical" )

searchDocs.title: Planet and moon technology icons​
searchDocs.content: These helpers build technology icons arrays in the style of vanilla planet- and moon-discovery technologies. They accept a sprite path for your technology icon.

searchDocs.title: PlanetsLib.technology_icon_planet(tech_icon, icon_size, shadow_scale)​
searchDocs.content: Returns an array of IconData: your technology icon with the vanilla constant-planet overlay in the corner. The base layout comes from util.technology_icon_constant_planet.  tech_icon — string — sprite path of your technology icon.icon_size — integer — optional size of tech_icon in pixels. Defaults to 256.shadow_scale — number — optional. When provided, a __PlanetsLib__/graphics/icons/planet-technology.png symbol is added first and the list is reordered to symbol, your icon (scaled by shadow_scale * 128 / icon_size and shifted {0, 10}), then the constant-planet overlay. When omitted, no shadow or planet symbol is drawn.

searchDocs.title: PlanetsLib.technology_icon_moon(tech_icon, icon_size, shadow_scale)​
searchDocs.content: Identical to PlanetsLib.technology_icon_planet, except that the final overlay is replaced with the moon symbol __PlanetsLib__/graphics/icons/moon-technology-symbol.png. It takes the same arguments.  local tech = data.raw.technology["my-planet-discovery"] tech.icon = nil tech.icon_size = nil tech.icons = PlanetsLib.technology_icon_planet("__my-mod__/graphics/technology/planet.png", 256, 0.5)

searchDocs.title: PlanetsLib.technology_icons_planet_cargo_drops(planet_icon, icon_size, mini)​
searchDocs.content: Returns an array of four IconData entries used for cargo-drop technologies: the cargo-pod icon, the planet icon, a semi-transparent black shadow, and the cargo-pod icon again.  planet_icon — string — sprite path of the planet icon.icon_size — integer — optional size of planet_icon in pixels. Defaults to 256. The planet is scaled by 0.65 * 256 / icon_size.mini — boolean — optional. When true, the planet icon is centred instead of being shifted { -17, 55 }.  This function is normally used indirectly through PlanetsLib.cargo_drops_technology_base(planet, planet_technology_icon, planet_technology_icon_size).

searchDocs.title: Related cargo-drop helpers​
searchDocs.content: PlanetsLib.cargo_drops_technology_base(planet, planet_technology_icon, planet_technology_icon_size) returns a complete cargo-drop technology prototype named planetslib-<planet>-cargo-drops. Its icons field comes from technology_icons_planet_cargo_drops, and its effects come from technology_effect_cargo_drops. All three arguments are required; planet is a planet name.  PlanetsLib.technology_effect_cargo_drops(planet_name, icons) returns a single-element technology.effects array of type "nothing". It displays icons (an array of IconData) and a translated cargo-drop description referring to planet_name.

searchDocs.title: Backwards-compatible aliases​
searchDocs.content: The following aliases are still exported for compatibility with existing mods. Prefer the canonical names in new code.  PlanetsLib.technology_icons_moon — alias for PlanetsLib.technology_icon_moon.PlanetsLib.technology_icon_constant_planet — alias for PlanetsLib.technology_icon_planet.

searchDocs.title: Blurring technology icons​
searchDocs.content: PlanetsLib.blur_technology_icon(icons, blurriness) — Returns an array of IconData that appears blurred, by layering many nearly-transparent, slightly offset duplicates of every entry using a multiplicative-with-alpha blend mode. The original icons are not modified.  This is useful for increasing the apparent resolution of icons without modifying the source image.  icons — an array of IconData — the icons to blur.blurriness — number — how far the offset duplicates are displaced. Must be greater than 0; larger values produce a wider blur.  data.raw.technology["my-hidden-technology"].icons = PlanetsLib.blur_technology_icon({ { icon = "__my-mod__/graphics/technology/thing.png", icon_size = 128 } }, 8)

searchDocs.title: Hardcoded Special Properties​
searchDocs.content: PlanetsLib reserves two special property values for runtime scripts set up during data-final-fixes. They are displayed as surface properties in game. If no mods define these properties, they are not displayed.  rocket_lift_multiplier(float) — Multiplies the lift of every rocket silo placed on the planet. Achieved via runtime entity replacements generated during data-final-fixes(See Planet-Exclusive Entity Variants).rocket_part_multiplier(float) — Multiplies the rocket parts required of every rocket silo placed on the planet. Achieved via the runtime entity replacements.

searchDocs.title: Surface conditions​
searchDocs.content: New surface properties​  PlanetsLib includes a variety of surface properties, all of which are either hidden or disabled by default. To enable a surface property, modders must add the following line to settings-updates.lua (using 'oxygen' as an example):  data.raw["bool-setting"]["PlanetsLib-enable-oxygen"].forced_value = true  Planet string limitation​  The legacy planet-string surface property (planet-str) and the parent-planet-str surface property encode a planet name in a double. Only names of six characters or fewer are guaranteed to round-trip; seven- and eight-character names can be truncated or corrupted because a double only has 53 bits of integer precision. This affects the legacy PlanetsLib.restrict_to_surface helper. Prefer PlanetsLib.restrict_to_planet when possible, because it uses a dedicated hidden surface property instead of encoding the planet name.  Restricting and relaxing conditions​  Typically, when planet mods want to modify a surface condition, what they are trying to do is restrict or relax the range of values for which that recipe or entity is allowed.  For example, Space Age recyclers have a maximum magnetic field of 99. If mod A wants to allow recyclers to be built up to 120, whilst mod B wants to allow them up to 150, compatibility issues can arise if mod A acts last and overrides mod B's change (which it ought to have been perfectly happy with). Instead mod A should modify existing surface conditions only if necessary.  Hence relax_surface_conditions and restrict_surface_conditions are provided, used like so:  PlanetsLib.relax_surface_conditions(data.raw.recipe["recycler"], {property = "magnetic-field", max = 120})PlanetsLib.restrict_surface_conditions(data.raw.recipe["boiler"], {property = "pressure", min = 10})  NOTE: Calling relax_surface_conditions without a min field will not remove any existing min conditions for that property (and similarly for max).  Removing surface conditions​  PlanetsLib.remove_surface_condition(recipe_or_entity, "magnetic-field") — Removes all magnetic-field surface conditions.PlanetsLib.remove_surface_condition(recipe_or_entity, {property = "magnetic-field", max = 120}) — Removes all surface conditions that exactly match the provided condition.

searchDocs.title: Usage​
searchDocs.content: -- data.lua, data-updates.lua, or data-final-fixes.lua PlanetsLib.assign_entity_removal_floor("muluna", { "lunar-rock", "lunar-huge-rock" }, "muluna-gravel", { default_tile_item = "stone-crushed", })   PlanetsLib.assign_entity_removal_floor(planet, entities, default_tile, options) configures the mechanic:  planet — Planet name or planet prototype. Only surfaces whose LuaSurface.planet matches this planet use the rule.entities — One entity name, an array of names, or a dictionary of name to true. The entities must exist and have a supported prototype type: simple-entity, plant, tree, or container.default_tile — Preferred tile prototype placed under the entity. It must not have destroys_dropped_items set, or the floor would destroy the same drops it is meant to protect. PlanetsLib verifies that the tile can actually be built on each unsafe footprint tile; if the default cannot be built there, another buildable safe tile is chosen.options (optional): default_tile_item — Item used to place default_tile. If omitted, PlanetsLib finds an item whose place_as_tile result is default_tile. When no such item exists, players cannot fall back to another tile.waiting_message — Localised string shown when a queued entity is marked for deconstruction again. Defaults to a PlanetsLib message.  Calling the function again for the same planet/entity pair replaces the older rule. PlanetsLib.add_entity_removal_floor_rule() is an alias.

searchDocs.title: Behaviour​
searchDocs.content: When one of the configured entities is marked for deconstruction:  PlanetsLib checks every tile in the entity's whole-tile footprint.If every tile is safe, the deconstruction order is left alone.Otherwise, PlanetsLib cancels the order, queues the entity, and places tile ghosts of the replacement tile under the unsafe tiles.When the floor has been built, the deconstruction order is reissued. Construction robots can then deconstruct the entity without destroying its drops.If construction robots built the temporary floor, it is ordered for deconstruction after the entity is gone and its dropped items have been picked up. Floors built by a player are left in place.  Character players who are outside a stationary roboport network and do not carry enough of the rule's default_tile_item may use another tile item from their inventory, provided it places a safe tile that is buildable on the footprint tile. The rule's default_tile is used when no suitable fallback exists.  Undoing the deconstruction order removes the queued entry and any tile ghosts that PlanetsLib created for it.

searchDocs.title: Mod-data format​
searchDocs.content: The API writes into the Planetslib mod-data prototype's entity_removal_floors table. Mods may also write the table directly:  data.raw["mod-data"].Planetslib.data.entity_removal_floors["muluna"] = { ["lunar-rock"] = { default_tile = "muluna-gravel", default_tile_item = "stone-crushed", }, ["lunar-huge-rock"] = { default_tile = "muluna-gravel", default_tile_item = "stone-crushed", }, }   The runtime also accepts a grouped form, where a rule has its own entities list:  data.raw["mod-data"].Planetslib.data.entity_removal_floors["muluna"] = { { entities = { "lunar-rock", "lunar-huge-rock" }, default_tile = "muluna-gravel", default_tile_item = "stone-crushed", }, }   Because both the data-stage API and the runtime read the same mod-data table, rules added during data-final-fixes are available when the game starts.

searchDocs.title: Known limitations​
searchDocs.content: The mechanic only applies to entities whose prototype type is simple-entity, plant, tree, or container. Corpses and other entity types are ignored.Tile ghosts are placed in the entity's whole-tile footprint, using the entity's bounding_box rather than its placement grid. Entities with unusual collision shapes can therefore receive a larger floor than their visual footprint.The temporary floor is not transferred if a mod or script replaces the queued entity with a different entity before deconstruction; the queue keeps tracking the original entity.

searchDocs.title: Event Handler
searchDocs.content: Event Handler Planetslib provides an alternative to the event handler library found in factorio's core mod, the core of the code was taken from there then extended. It does work as a drop in replacement for that. Filtering:​ The add_filter(event,filter) method can add a filter to every registered event handler. The filters are added to all of your handlers, if you use a filter in one spot then use the same event elsewhere then you need to add the filters for that event as well. This is not done on the lua side, this interacts with the engine's event filters. You still need to do a check in the function if you filter for multiple entities in your mod, and they don't have the same behavior. local handler = require("__PlanetsLib__.lib.event-handler.event-handler") -- all built events will get this filter handler.add_filter(defines.events.on_built_entity,{ filter="name", name="orbital-cannon" }) handler.add_lib(require("script.orbital-cannon")) Composite events:​ Some frequently used event combinations can be declared together. You have to write the handler in a way that supports all included events. on_built: Every event that could fire when a new entity was built.on_removed: Every event when the entity was mined or destroyed. local handler = require("__PlanetsLib__.lib.event-handler.event-handler") -- include the built in "on_built" and "on_removed" composite events handler.add_composite_events(require("__PlanetsLib__.lib.event-handler.composite-events")) -- using the name of a composite event is also valid for a filter, it will apply to every included event. handler.add_filter("on_built",{ filter="name", name="orbital-cannon" }) --in your handler code local lib = { composite_events = { on_built= function(event) end, on_removed= function(event) end } } return lib Remote interface:​ The add_to_remote_interface method lets you append to a single remote interface that is registered with your mod's name, instead of either collecting all of you api functions from every relevant file, or registering multiple remote interfaces. local handler = require("__PlanetsLib__.lib.event-handler.event-handler") local function api_function() end local lib ={ add_to_remote_interface = function(interface) interface["api_function"] = api_function end } handler.add_lib(lib) Can be called as: remote.call("your mod", "api_function")

searchDocs.title: Player Facing Features
searchDocs.content: Player Facing Features The primary intent of PlanetsLib is to be a library which provides opt-in functionality for other mods. However, a small number of game-affecting or player-interface-affecting features have been added over time. These are listed below, player feedback on them is most welcome in Discord. Unlinking hidden prerequisites If PlanetsLib detects that technologies have hidden prerequisites such that they would be unresearchable, it warns players about this fact. This is done because the Factorio client gives no explanation or reason for why these technologies cannot be researched.There are PlanetsLib mod settings to repair the user's game by unlinking all such prerequisites, or to disable the warning.If the repair list (unlinked_prerequisites) is non-empty, PlanetsLib warns about the repairs instead of also showing the hidden-prerequisite warning; the repair warning takes precedence. Fixed rocket weights of vanilla items If an item prototype does not have an explicitly specified rocket weight, the behavior of the Factorio engine is to assign it a weight based on the recipes that produce it. Unfortunately, this means that the rocket weight of vanilla items is liable to change when additional mods are installed. PlanetsLib therefore sets an explicit weight on vanilla items equal to their weight in Space Age. This occurs in data-final-fixes and only if the item does not have a weight by that point. Extra informational tooltips On recipes: Freshness resets on craft completion This tracks result_is_always_fresh and only appears if true. Freshness resets on craft beginning This tracks reset_freshness_on_craft and only appears if true. Products preserved in machine output This tracks preserve_products_in_machine_output and only appears if true. All such tooltips are added in data-final-fixes. Biolab inputs Because modders often forget about the Biolab when adding a new science pack, PlanetsLib mirrors all science packs from the vanilla lab to the Biolab in data-final-fixes. Centrifuge entity improvements This entity is given an input and an output fluidbox (or two of each if the mod setting PlanetsLib-enable-additional-centrifuge-fluidboxes is enabled).Also, the graphics of the working glow are improved so that it naturally glows different colors depending on the recipe. Space platform hub improvements The list of cargo pods that can be accepted by the vanilla space platform hub can be modifying by modifying PlanetsLib.constants.space_platform_hub_receiving_cargo_units. The global functions platform_upper_hatch and platform_lower_hatch added by base Space Age are overridden and modified by PlanetsLib to reference mod-data tables from PlanetsLib. Space tile without the ability to cover it A space tile that can be used around limited surfaces floating in space, as it can not be covered in space platform tiles. Modders, enable it with the PlanetsLib-enable-blocking-empty-space-tile setting. The name of the tile is planetslib-empty-space, all localization is set to match the regular empty-space tile from space age.

searchDocs.title: Entity variant migrations​
searchDocs.content: On adding new entity replacement rules to an existing save, disabling old replacement rules, or removing rules entirely from the rule table, PlanetsLib will perform a runtime migration on all entities in violation of the current ruleset to comply with the new ruleset. This process includes copying the settings, wire connections, inventories, fluidbox contents, health, crafting progress, and a myriad of other settings associated with entities. This process is not perfect, so reports of incomplete migrations are welcome.  A save records the entity names used by its rules. If a mod update removes one of those prototypes (for example a generated "<entity>-PlanetsLib-<planet>" variant), migration skips and logs the affected rule instead of failing to load the save.

searchDocs.title: Safely disabling an entity replacement rule​
searchDocs.content: Each entity replacement rule must be associated with a startup setting, defined with bound_setting. When this setting is enabled, entity replacements are active. When this setting is disabled, variant entities are generated in data, allowing saves with obsolete rules to load without deleting any entities. However, on loading a save, all variant entities that should not exist under the current ruleset are replaced with their original entity, reverting all replacements performed under that rule.  To safely remove an entity replacement from the game, disable the associated startup setting, load the save to allow the migration to occur, then remove the mod. When updating a mod to revert an entity replacement rule, apply a conventional migration to all affected entities, or if not possible, hide and force disable the associated setting, rather than deleting code adding the replacement rule. After you are ready to make old saves break their migration, you can delete the associated code.  PlanetsLib also exposes the player-facing startup setting PlanetsLib-disable-all-entity-replacements. It overrides every rule's own bound_setting: when it is enabled, no replacement is performed at runtime and migrations do not replace entities. This is a global emergency switch for players; mods should keep using their own bound_setting for normal uninstallation.

searchDocs.title: Making your entity compatible with PlanetsLib's entity replacement script​
searchDocs.content: If you have a script-augmented entity and a PlanetsLib entity replacement targets your entity, PlanetsLib.constants.entity_variants_list contains a list of entity variants for each entity. For scripted entity "scripted_entity", A list of variant entities will be found in PlanetsLib.constants.entity_variants_list["scripted_entity"] if any exist. To make your script-augmented entity compatible, add entities from this list to any entity name checks in your control stage. If PlanetsLib replaces an entity tracked in your mod's storage, remote.call("planetslib_entity_replacement","get_replacement",entity_unit_number) will return the LuaEntity that replaced your entity. Use this function to repair stale references.  Custom event: PlanetsLib.events.on_entity_replaced(event)Runs when PlanetsLib replaces an entity. Use this event to change variables associated with script-augmented entities to refer to the new entity.event fields: entity(LuaEntity): The entity about to be deleted.new_entity(LuaEntity): The entity that has had entity's settings and inventory transferred to.

searchDocs.title: Appendix​
searchDocs.content: PlanetsLib.create_planet_entity_variant steps​  PlanetsLib.create_planet_entity_variant(planet_names,entity,new_properties,bound_setting,item_name)  This section describes the steps taken by create_planet_entity_variant to help explain possible incompatibilities.  On calling function in data stage:  Generate a deepcopy of entity. This will be named new_entity.Append "-PlanetsLib-{first_planet}" to new_entity's name, giving it a unique name. If planet_names is a string, first_planet is planet_names. If it is a table, first_planet is planet_names[1].Set the fields of new_entity such that the external appearance of new_entity is the same as entity. This includes copying entity's localised_name and localised_description, redirecting Factoriopedia requests to entity, hiding new_entity from Factoriopedia, adding entity flags hiding the entity from "made-in" and from the bonus gui, and overriding placeable_by to be item_name. If item_name is undefined and data.raw["item"][entity.name] exists, item_name will use this item.While it's possible to almost fully hide the existence of variant entities, they will still appear in upgrade planners. To make variant entity icons visually distinct from their original, the sprite of the planet this variant entity is intended for will be added to the top right corner of the variant entity's icon.To allow additional customization, new_entity and new_properties will be merged into one table, with each top-level key in new_properties overriding the value of the same top-level key.Using PlanetsLib.assign_entity_replacement, new_entity is registered as a replacement for entity on each planet in planet_names if it's a list, or on planet_names if it is not a list. This tells PlanetsLib's control script "If entity placed on this planet, delete it and replace it with new_entity." The rule's enabled field is set from bound_setting: if the setting is disabled, the rule is still registered with enabled = false so existing variants can be migrated back when a save loads.new_entity is added to data.raw. By default, it also has PlanetsLib_do_not_generate_variants = true, so other PlanetsLib variant generators skip it; new_properties may override this flag for those generators. PlanetsLib.create_planet_entity_variant always ignores entities that are already generated variants, identified by the flag or by the generated -PlanetsLib- name suffix, even if the flag was overridden. This makes it safe to call the function while iterating a prototype table, for example for _, panel in pairs(data.raw["solar-panel"]): the variants created during the loop are not used to create further variants.  In control stage:  On configuration changed:  If any entity replacement rules have changed since last save. Perform a migration.During a migration, each entity replacement rule is evaluated, and entities on each surface not matching the rule are replaced. If the rule is not enabled by the user, reverse replacements made by the rule. If the rule is enabled, perform replacements that should have been made by the rule.  On placing entity:  On placing an entity on planet, if PlanetsLib.constants. on_entity_placed_on_planet_replacements[planet][entity] exists, this tells PlanetsLib that entity is intended to be replaced on planet.If enabled == true, execute the rule, replacing entity with new_entity.Transfer settings, inventory, and other information from the old entity to the new entity.

searchDocs.title: Recipe productivity technology helper field​
searchDocs.content: PlanetsLib adds a new field named PlanetsLib_recipe_productivity_effects to TechnologyPrototype, used by recipe productivity technologies. During data-final-fixes, technologies with this field will have their effects list appended or replaced with recipes matching either an output name or recipe category. Recipes will be excluded if they have the field PlanetsLib_blacklist_technology_updates set to true.  Recipe products are ignored if they are not "productivity-capable"—if ignored_by_productivity is greater than or equal to amount (or amount_max)—because changing a recipe's productivity has no effect on such products. If a recipe has no productivity-capable products, it is fully ineligible; and if a recipe has multiple products, but only one product is productivity-capable (e.g. Kovarex enrichment), it is eligible even if allow_multiple_results = false.  If a technology with PlanetsLib_recipe_productivity_effects defined (and valid) has no effects after PlanetsLib has finished processing it, the technology is excised using PlanetsLib.excise_tech_from_tech_tree unless PlanetsLib_recipe_productivity_effects.force_do_not_excise is set to true.  TechnologyPrototype field: PlanetsLib_recipe_productivity_effects Properties:​  effects: table[ChangeResultProductivityModifier]category_blacklist - table[RecipeCategoryID]. Recipes in these categories are skipped. Defaults to { "recycling" }. Must be omitted when using a category filter.purge_other_effects- boolean. Default: false. Before adding effects added by PlanetsLib_recipe_productivity_effects, remove all effects not flagged with PlanetsLib_force_include.allow_recipes_without_productivity - boolean. Default: false. Captures recipes even if they have allow_productivity set to false.force_do_not_excise - boolean. Default: false. Does not automatically excise this technology even if it has no effects.technology_name - string. If this field is defined, PlanetsLib_recipe_productivity_effects does not apply if this field is not equal to the technology name. Acts as a check to prevent deepcopies of vanilla recipe productivity technologies from unknowingly receiving these effects.  ChangeResultProductivityModifier Properties:​  name (optional) - ItemID Required if not using category. Incompatible with category.type (optional) - ProductPrototype Required if using name.category (optional) - RecipeCategoryID Required if not using name. Incompatible with name and category_blacklist.allow_multiple_results: boolean. Default: false. When false, only recipes with one (productivity-capable) result are added to the technology's effect list. If multiple results have the same name, they are counted as a single result rather than being counted individually.  Inherited from ChangeRecipeProductivityModifier​  changeicons (optional)icon (optional)icon_size (optional)hidden (optional)use_icon_overlay_constant (optional)  New BaseModifier field: PlanetsLib_force_include​  Makes this modifier immune to purge_other_effects.  New RecipePrototype field: PlanetsLib_blacklist_technology_updates​  Stops PlanetsLib from targeting this recipe in technology updates.  Example​  { type = "technology", name = "thruster-fuel-productivity", --Other required fields here PlanetsLib_recipe_productivity_effects = { purge_other_effects = true, effects = { { type = "fluid", name = "thruster-fuel", change = 0.1 }, { type = "fluid", name = "thruster-oxidizer", change = 0.1 }, } } }     Tech tree adjustments​  PlanetsLib.excise_tech_from_tech_tree(tech_name) — Seamlessly removes a technology from the tech tree by making all its dependencies depend instead on the technology's prerequisites. In addition, hidden = true is set on the technology.PlanetsLib.excise_recipe_from_tech_tree(recipe_name, include_productivity_effects) — Removes unlocking this recipe from all technologies. If include_productivity_effects is true, also removes any productivity effects of this recipe from all technologies (if called before data-final-fixes, also adds PlanetsLib_blacklist_technology_updates = true to the recipe). If the effect removal(s) leave any technology with zero effects, the technology is excised using PlanetsLib.excise_tech_from_tech_tree.PlanetsLib.excise_effect_from_tech_tree(effect) — Similar to excise_recipe_from_tech_tree, but any effect can be passed. Example: PlanetsLib.excise_effect_from_tech_tree({ type = "unlock-quality", quality = "uncommon" }) PlanetsLib.add_science_packs_from_vanilla_lab_to_technology(technology) — Adds all science packs that the vanilla lab have slots for to the unit of the given technology. Can be useful when defining endgame technologies.
